$description: Open-licensed font catalogue for the UI Suite. Stores what helps you PICK a face, not just its name. Nothing here is bundled yet — this is the shortlist, see notes.verify.

notes.license: Every entry is SIL Open Font License 1.1: free to use, modify, bundle and ship inside a commercial product. The only restriction is you cannot sell the font on its own. Public Sans is US government work, also OFL.
notes.verify: Confirm the license file at download time. Foundries occasionally relicense, and a repo you redistribute from is the wrong place to be wrong.
notes.formats: Ship WOFF2 for web (~30% smaller than TTF, universally supported). Keep TTF/OTF for desktop app targets — GTK, WinUI and Qt read those, not WOFF2.
notes.variable: Prefer variable fonts. One file carries every weight, so a variable family usually beats shipping even two static weights on total bytes.
notes.xHeight: Qualitative, not measured. High x-height stays legible at small UI sizes; low x-height reads better at large display sizes. Judged by eye, not by tooling — treat as a hint, not data.
notes.science: Legibility properties here (x-height, counters, character differentiation) are backed by real reading research. The 'personality' of a face is genre convention, not intrinsic meaning — same caveat as colour, see references/palettes.md.

Inter.caution: The most-used UI sans on the web and the default 'AI-generated' look. Excellent face, zero distinctiveness.

Public Sans.caution: Deliberately neutral. Reads as institutional, which is sometimes exactly wrong.

Manrope.caution: No true italic — the browser will synthesise a slant, which looks cheap at large sizes.

Archivo.note: Variable axis includes width, so condensed and expanded come from the same file.

Barlow.caution: Not variable — you ship one file per weight.

Literata.note: Drawn for screen reading specifically — higher x-height than most text serifs.

EB Garamond.caution: Low x-height. Beautiful large, muddy below ~15px.

JetBrains Mono.note: Tall x-height and hard character differentiation; optional ligatures.

IBM Plex Mono.note: Part of the Plex superfamily — Sans and Serif siblings share skeletons, so mixing them looks intentional.

Space Mono.caution: A display mono, not a work mono. Painful for long code.

Fraunces.note: Variable axes include softness and 'wonk'. Very expressive — headlines only.

Instrument Serif.caution: One weight only. Display sizes exclusively.
